reference_title: Assuring Quality in Geotechnical Reporting Documents
chapter_title: Content and Quality Assurance of Geotechnical Reporting Documents

sections.title: GRD Content and QA Requirements
sections.summary: GRDs must communicate — not merely summarize — site conditions and design/construction recommendations. Minimum GRD content per FHWA (2003): subsurface exploration data (profile, logs, lab/in situ results, GWT), interpretation and analysis, specific engineering recommendations, conditions for anticipated problems, recommended geotechnical special provisions. Suggested format: title page, TOC, executive summary, introduction, procedures/results (field + lab), summary of analyses, discussion, recommendations, construction recommendations, figures, appendices. GS must review final plans and specifications to verify recommendations are properly incorporated before acceptance by owner.
sections.body:
Purposes of GRDs: (1) project programming — establish scope for projects with significant geotechnical features; (2) provide management and owners understanding of geotechnical impacts on cost and schedule; (3) provide design disciplines with information needed for their designs; (4) provide contractors information for competitive bids with acceptable risk; (5) provide construction staff with knowledge of subsurface conditions; (6) provide owners with documentation of contractor meeting minimum investigation and design requirements.

GRD forms and formats: Comprehensive GRs (common for DBB); GRs focused on one design phase (preliminary, intermediate, final); GRs focused on one design element (bridge, retaining wall); GDRs for DB bid phase (factual only); GBRs for tunnels (contractually binding baseline); memos or emails for quick documentation of a single element or modification (especially useful for DB projects).

Minimum GRD content (FHWA 2003): subsurface exploration data including soil/rock profile, exploratory logs, lab or in-situ test results, and groundwater information; interpretation and analysis of subsurface data; specific engineering recommendations for design; discussion of conditions for solution of anticipated problems; recommended geotechnical special provisions.

Suggested format (FHWA 2007): Title Page, Table of Contents, Executive Summary, Introduction, Procedures and Results (field investigations + laboratory testing), Summary of Analyses, Discussion (geology, seismicity, geologic hazards), Recommendations (design and construction), Construction Recommendations (observations, testing, instrumentation), Figures, Appendices (boring logs, in situ results, lab results, others).

QC/QA distinction: QC = independent checking and verification to ensure final product meets requirements. QA = the actions necessary to create confidence that QC has occurred. These two definitions are consistent across multiple DOTs. QC reviewer must understand technical details; QA reviewer maintains broader project view.

Critical GRD communications: 'One of the more important words in the GRD definition is communicate, which means something much more than summarize.' GRD must be reviewed with design engineers for all disciplines. GS must review final plans and specifications to verify recommendations have been properly incorporated before acceptance by owner.
key_points: GRD must 'communicate' — not just summarize; review with design engineers for all disciplines is essential
Minimum content: subsurface data, interpretation, recommendations, conditions, special provisions
GS must review final PS&E to verify recommendations were properly incorporated before construction
QC = independent technical checking; QA = confirming QC has been done
Analyses/computations must be prepared and available upon request even if not all included in GRD
sections.applicability: Required content, format, and QA expectations for geotechnical reporting documents

sections.title: Applications to Alternative Contracting Methods
sections.summary: GRDs required at each phase of each ACM: DBB (planning, preliminary design, intermediate, final structure, final roadway, ATC/VE reports); DB (planning, preliminary GRD, GDR for bid, interim GRDs per element, final structure/roadway GRDs); CM/GC (planning, preliminary, interim GRDs, final structure/roadway GRDs). Owner agency must institute procedures for geotechnical investigations and QA requirements for all ACMs, referencing AASHTO, FHWA, and/or their own manuals.
sections.body:
GRDs by ACM phase:

Design-Bid-Build (DBB): Planning, Preliminary Design, Intermediate Design, Final Structure/Bridge Design, Final Design or Final Roadway Design (if separate structure report prepared), Report for ATC or VE Study.

Design-Build (DB): Planning, Preliminary Design, Geotechnical Data Report (GDR), Intermediate GRDs for project elements or parts of project, Final Structure/Bridge Design summarizing all structures/bridges, Final Roadway Design summarizing all roadway elements.

Construction Manager/General Contractor (CM/GC): Planning, Preliminary Design, Intermediate GRDs for project elements, Final Structure/Bridge Design, Final Roadway Design.

In each case, the owner agency should institute procedures for geotechnical investigations whether utilizing their own manual or by reference to AASHTO, FHWA, etc. Required QC and QA procedures should also be in place. QA for technical features based on checklists. A QA Audit by the owner agency verifies QA reviews were completed.
key_points: DBB: planning through final design GRDs; may include ATC or VE GRD
DB: owner provides GDR (factual) for bid phase; DB Team prepares final design GRDs after selection
CM/GC: same GRD sequence as DBB with contractor input during design
Owner agency must institute investigation procedures and QA requirements for all ACMs
sections.applicability: GRD requirements for Design-Bid-Build, Design-Build, and CM/GC contracting methods
